$$
\ba
\ey
&\eqdef \eExp{Y \mid \vX = \vx, T = t} \\
&\quad \text{(definition of estimated conditional expectation)} \\
&= \emu(\vx, t) \\
&\quad \text{(estimated mean count function)} \\
&= \el(\vx) \cdot t \\
&\quad \text{(substituting the estimated rate relation)} \\
&= \exp{\est{\eta}(\vx)} \cdot t \\
&\quad \text{(substituting the inverse link function)} \\
&= \exp{\eb_0 + \eb_1 x_1 + \dots + \eb_p x_p} \cdot t \\
&\quad \text{(substituting estimated linear predictor } \est{\eta}(\vx)\text{)}
\ea
$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-pois-two-group-pred}
#### Predicted count for a new exposed cohort

Using the two-cohort fit from @exm-pois-two-group-mle,
the predicted number of events
for a new exposed cohort ($x = 1$)
followed for $t = 1000$ person-years is:

$$
\ba
\ey
&= \expf{\eb_0 + \eb_1} \cdot t
&& \text{(fitted mean function)} \\
&= \el(1) \cdot 1000
&& \text{(fitted rate for } x = 1 \text{)} \\
&= 0.006 \cdot 1000
&& \text{(substitute the fitted rate)} \\
&= 6
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
predict(
  fit_two_cohorts,
  newdata = data.frame(exposed = 1, person_years = 1000),
  type = "response"
)
```

:::
